subject: Deployment evaluation: Dedicated sizing follow-ups (GPU choice, TPS, token mix)
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@orchid.ai>

Cc: Samira Patel <samira.p@orchid.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood demo follow-up — deployment & sizing questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo today — Samira and I appreciated the clarity on fallbacks and the cost/latency trade-offs. We left with a couple of concrete asks so we can decide whether to pilot on Dedicated or stick with Hosted for now. Quick summary: 

- Primary workload: user-facing chat + retrieval-augmented answers; 95th p95 latency target: 300ms per API request (including network).
- Expected steady-state: 250 TPS of API calls at peak for single region; burst to 900 TPS for 10–15 minutes during marketing events.
- Token mix (approx): 70% short prompts (<80 tokens), 25% medium (80–400 tokens), 5% long (>400 tokens). Average output tokens per request ~120.
- Security: we need VPC option later; initial pilot can be in Dedicated (customer-isolated) but still on Redwood-managed infra.

Can you confirm what GPU SKUs you recommend for this profile, and whether the Dedicated pool can autoscale to handle the 900 TPS bursts without dropping below latency SLOs? Also attaching our token profile and a short capture of traffic for context.

Attachments: orchid_token_profile.csv, orchid_sample_traffic.pcap

Best,
Alex
Senior ML Engineer
Orchid AI

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up — deployment & sizing questions

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and for the attachments. Recap + next steps below.

Recap (short):
- Workload looks like a good fit for Redwood Dedicated as a pilot: consistent peak TPS and need for customer isolation later.
- Token mix skews short which helps latency; the 900 TPS burst is the main sizing challenge.

Questions / clarifications needed to size precisely:
1) Are the 250 / 900 TPS numbers measured at the API request level (i.e., one API call = one generation request)? Are you sending batched requests or one request per end-user action?
2) For the long requests (>400 tokens), are those mostly retrieval-augmented single-call generations, or multi-call flows that hold KV cache between calls?
3) What p95 latency budget is for the model inference alone vs. total API request (including your app-side network & retrieval)? You mentioned 300ms total; if inference must be <=200ms we may need different GPU choices.

Preliminary GPU guidance (high level):
- If inference budget for model alone is ~180–220ms and average sequence length ~220 tokens, we typically recommend an A100/80GB class or H100 depending on model (FP16/4-bit quantized).
- For tighter per-request latency (<150ms inference) with the same throughput, H100s with kernel-level optimizations and larger KV cache are better.
- We can mix GPU flavors in a Dedicated pool: H100s for low-latency steady allocation + A100s for background lower-priority work to smooth cost.

Autoscale and burst handling: yes — Dedicated pools can be configured with burst capacity and pre-warmed nodes. For a 900 TPS 10–15 minute event we typically use a buffer policy (pre-warm N nodes) + graceful scale-up so warmup latency is bounded. Need to agree on cost/commit model for burst capacity.

Next steps (proposed):
- Ben, can you sketch a baseline GPU mix and an estimate of nodes required for Priyom's numbers (250 steady / 900 burst, token mix attached)?
- Alex / Samira: confirm answers to the three clarifying questions above.
- I'll prepare a short Dedicated pilot SOW (2–4 week pilot) with burst/commit options and an estimated monthly cost range.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Priyom / Alex — quick sizing sketch based on the numbers provided. This is a back-of-envelope; I’ll follow with a short spreadsheet if this looks like the right direction.

Assumptions (from thread):
- Model: 30B-ish open model (FP16 / q4_0 or q4_K) — adjust if you're using a small LLM or a much larger one.
- Avg request tokens: prompt+response ~300 tokens (your split implies shorter prompts, but response ~120 avg).
- Target inference p95 budget: 200ms (model-only).

Baseline (steady 250 TPS):
- Single H100 (with optimized kernels) can handle ~400–600 TPS at short-token profiles depending on batching; practical steady capacity: 400 TPS. So 1 H100 could cover steady 250 TPS with room.
- A100 80GB (fp16) practical steady capacity: ~200–300 TPS depending on model and sequence length. You'd need 1–2 A100s for steady.

Burst (900 TPS for 10–15m):
- Pre-warm approach: reserve 1 H100 + 2 A100s permanently, and configure burst policy to add 2 more H100s for events. That brings burst capacity to ~1600 TPS theoretical, with headroom for concurrency spikes.
- Alternative cost-savvy: base of 2 A100s for steady, and on-demand H100s for event shortfalls; will trade some warm-up latency unless pre-warmed.

KV caching and batching notes:
- If you can reuse KV cache across subsequent calls (multi-turn conversations), effective throughput increases; share any multi-call flows.
- Continuous batching at the runtime level will aggregate same-latency requests — if bursts are sudden and synchronous (marketing event), ensure your burst policy pre-warms nodes to avoid queued latency.

Attachments: none from me yet — Priyom, I can drop a zoning spreadsheet in Drive and tag the expected node counts/resource hours.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. Answers below and one small ask.

Answers to clarification:
1) TPS numbers are API request level (one call per end-user action). We do not batch on the client side today.
2) Long requests (>400 tokens) are single-call retrieval-augmented generations (RAG) — we do not chain multiple generation calls for those. KV cache reuse happens for multi-turn chat flows (about 10% of traffic).
3) The 300ms p95 is app-level (end-to-end). We should target model inference p95 <= 200ms to leave headroom for retrieval/network.

Small ask: can you provide a short cost range for the two proposed pool mixes you mentioned (1) H100-heavy with pre-warm (H100s for low latency + A100s as background) and (2) A100-only with on-demand H100 burst? We don't need line-item legal pricing, just a ballpark monthly committed cost + estimated overage rate for burst.

Also attaching our security questionnaire for the pilot phase — we may need Redwood to confirm a few items for our security review.

Attachments: orchid_security_questions.pdf

If that looks good I think we can proceed to a pilot SOW — Samira will loop in procurement on our side once we have a ballpark.

Best,
Alex
Alex Wu
Senior ML Engineer, Orchid AI
